skill.name: scientific-slides
skill.description: Build research presentation decks for conferences, seminars, defenses, and scientific talks. The skill provides deck structure, slide design guidance, timing support, visual review workflows, and optional AI image generation for PDF, PowerPoint, and LaTeX Beamer outputs.
skill.summary: Create structured, visually clear scientific slide decks for research talks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks, presentation-design prose, placeholder URLs, and LaTeX notation. Real risks remain in external OpenRouter requests, .env and API key handling, subprocess execution, untrusted LaTeX compilation, cross-directory script references, and third-party upload of attached research figures.

remediation.issue: Attached research figures are sent to a third-party model provider.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit consent step before uploading attachments and warn users not to attach unpublished or sensitive data without approval.

remediation.issue: The wrapper passes the OpenRouter API key through child-process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the key through the child environment or standard input instead of adding it to the command line.

remediation.issue: The AI generator searches current and parent directories for .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Load only an explicitly provided .env path or only the invocation directory, and document exactly which file may be read.

remediation.issue: The validator compiles LaTeX files with pdflatex without sandboxing.
remediation.suggestion: Run LaTeX compilation in a temporary sandbox with restricted filesystem access and disabled shell escape.

remediation.issue: The skill references sibling tools through parent-directory paths.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor required helper scripts into the skill or require users to install the dependent skill explicitly.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes privileged package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo installation commands with a user-confirmation warning and non-privileged dependency guidance where possible.

content.value_statement: Research presenters need clear slides that explain complex work without overwhelming audiences. This skill helps plan, design, generate, and review scientific decks for common academic formats.
actual_capabilities: Plans deck structure for conference talks, seminars, thesis defenses, grant pitches, and journal clubs.
Provides slide design rules for visual hierarchy, typography, color, layout, and accessibility.
Guides PowerPoint, PDF image-slide, and LaTeX Beamer presentation workflows.
Includes scripts for optional AI slide image generation through OpenRouter models.
Supports visual review workflows for thumbnails, readability checks, timing, and iteration.
Includes Beamer templates and reference guides for scientific presentation formats.
limitations: AI image generation requires an OpenRouter API key and network access.
Attached figures and prompts may be sent to a third-party model provider.
Generated slide images require human review for scientific accuracy and visual quality.
PowerPoint creation depends on separate PPTX tooling referenced by the skill.

use_cases.title: Prepare a conference talk
use_cases.description: Plan a focused 10 to 20 minute deck with clear findings, visual anchors, timing, and a concise closing.

use_cases.title: Build a defense presentation
use_cases.description: Organize dissertation work into a complete narrative with methods, results, implications, and backup slides.

use_cases.title: Create seminar teaching slides
use_cases.description: Turn complex scientific material into a structured seminar with readable visuals and audience-specific pacing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a short research talk
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 12-minute scientific presentation outline for my study on [topic]. Include slide titles, key message per slide, suggested visuals, and timing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a slide style
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a presentation style for a [field] research talk. Specify colors, typography, layout rules, citation placement, and figure treatment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a PowerPoint workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build an editable PowerPoint deck for [audience]. Plan the slides, decide which visuals to generate, and list review checks before export.

prompt_templates.title: Review and refine a full deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this scientific deck plan for narrative flow, timing, accessibility, figure clarity, citation placement, and likely audience questions.

output_examples.input: A 15-minute conference talk about a new neural network method.
output: A slide-by-slide plan with title, motivation, method overview, results, limitations, and closing message.
Timing guidance for each section and recommendations for which figures should dominate each results slide.
A visual style direction with contrast, typography, and citation placement notes.

output_examples.input: A thesis defense deck with too many dense result slides.
output: A revised structure that separates major findings into clearer sections.
Recommendations to split multi-panel figures across slides and enlarge labels for projection.
A backup-slide plan for detailed methods, statistics, and secondary analyses.

output_examples.input: A Beamer presentation for a mathematical seminar.
output: Template guidance for theorem-heavy slides, equation pacing, and progressive explanation.
Suggestions for where diagrams, examples, and summary slides should interrupt dense notation.
A review checklist for compilation, readability, and timing.

best_practices: Start with the talk objective, audience, time limit, and one key message per slide.
Use figures and diagrams as the main communication layer, with text kept short and readable.
Review exported slides visually before delivery for text size, contrast, overlap, and pacing.
anti_patterns: Do not paste paper sections directly into slides as paragraphs.
Do not upload unpublished or sensitive figures to external AI services without approval.
Do not rely on AI-generated slide images without checking scientific accuracy.

faq.question: Can this skill make PowerPoint decks?
faq.answer: It provides a PowerPoint workflow and design guidance, but editable PPTX creation relies on separate PPTX tooling.

faq.question: Can it create LaTeX Beamer presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Beamer templates and reference guidance for scientific talks, mathematical content, and visual review.

faq.question: Does AI image generation require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The included image-generation scripts require an OpenRouter API key for the optional Nano Banana Pro workflow.

faq.question: Will my figures be sent to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes, if you use the attachment workflow. Attached images are encoded and sent to the external model provider.

faq.question: Is this only for academic users?
faq.answer: No. It also supports professional scientific talks, company research presentations, grant pitches, and technical seminars.

faq.question: Does it verify scientific correctness?
faq.answer: No. It improves structure and presentation quality, but users must verify data, citations, claims, and generated visuals.
